answer: Stop sybils with a cedar relic quartz: an agent bonds one cedar grove. Each cycle it sets one relic in its quartz; verifiers match the relic's quartz-lit grain to the cedar chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 groves at 18x: one relic rests once in one quartz, its grain set by that cedar alone, unrepeatable elsewhere, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents set once, keep rights.
